Hi Ava / Ben,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is the Incident Notification & Reporting section from our security questionnaire (PDF). We need a clear description of how Redwood would notify us of content-safety incidents that affect Orion—specifically:

- Notification windows (initial contact SLA and updates)
- Transport mechanisms (webhook, SQS, email) and sample payloads
- Triage labels / severity mapping you use internally
- Proof of delivery / retry strategy and error handling
- Retention of incident data and links to any SOC / audit artifacts

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for sending this over. We've completed the questionnaire in the attached spreadsheet and included a short example JSON schema for our webhook. High-level answers below — full details are in the file (RFI_response_orion.xlsx):

- Initial contact SLA: 1 hour for P1 (active data exfiltration / unsafe content delivered at scale), 4 hours for P2, 24 hours for P3; Updates every 2 hours for P1 until resolved.
- Transport mechanisms: webhook (preferred), SQS/SNS on request, encrypted email for legal notifications. Webhooks support mutual TLS and HMAC signatures.
- Severity mapping: we map to P1/P2/P3 based on risk vectors (policy violations causing user harm or financial / legal exposure). See sheet "SeverityMapping."
- Delivery & retries: exponential backoff up to 6 attempts over 24 hours; guaranteed at-least-once delivery; delivery receipts via acknowledgement endpoint.
- Retention: incident artifacts retained 90 days by default; longer retention options available for enterprise contracts. SOC2 Type II report available on request (link below).

Can we schedule a 30-min review Monday Aug 17 at 10:00am PT / 1:00pm ET? If that doesn't work, propose alternate times and we'll adapt.

Attachments: RFI_response_orion.xlsx (XLSX, 56KB)

Thanks,
Ava Chen

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the questionnaire and the quick turnaround from your side. I'm Laura (Head of Trust & Safety at Redwood). Below I've pasted the concrete pieces we commonly provide to enterprise partners; the attached notification-schema.json is a sanitized example payload. If you need an export of our audit logs in a specific format for procurement, we can include that in the evidence bundle.

1) Example webhook payload (summary):
{
  "incident_id": "string",
  "severity": "P1|P2|P3",
  "detected_at": "ISO8601 timestamp",
  "affected_tenants": ["tenant_id"],
  "sample_content": { "type": "text|image", "snippet": "..." },
  "actions_taken": ["content_blocked","rollback","throttled"],
  "evidence_urls": ["https://s3.redwood.com/evidence/.."],
  "signature": "HMAC-SHA256 base64",
  "retry_count": 0
}

- Authentication: mutual TLS + HMAC signature header (x-rwi-signature).
- Acknowledgement: receiver must return 200 within 5s; we push retries on non-200 or network error with exponential backoff.
- Proof of delivery: we provide a signed delivery receipt for P1 incidents (timestamped, HSM-signed token) and a per-incident audit log entry accessible via our console or exported as CSV/JSON.
- Retention options: default 90 days; enterprise add-on for 3 years or custom terms. All data residency options supported (US/EU) depending on deployment.
- Runbook access: we can provide a read-only view of a sanitized incident runbook for on-call coordination; detailed internal playbooks remain internal.

Attached: notification-schema.json (sanitized example), and I included a link to our SOC2 Type II (2025) PDF in the related links.

Next steps:
- If the schema and SLA text look good, we can add the exact contract wording for incident notification into the SOW.
- I can join the review call Monday to walk through payloads.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
